issues.description: The problem specification is inconsistent about the type of the Farm.animals collection: the UML diagram shows animals: List<Animal> while the textual instructions explicitly require using a Set (HashSet) to ensure uniqueness. The provided solution implements a List (ArrayList), and the template does not define the collection. This mismatch (UML vs. textual requirement vs. solution) will confuse students about whether to use a List or a Set and whether uniqueness is required.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the intended collection type explicit and consistent across all artifacts. Prefer one of two fixes:
1) If uniqueness is required (as the text states), update the UML to show animals: Set<Animal>, update the solution to use Set<Animal> (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();) and update the template to include this field and constructor initializing the HashSet. Adjust iteration code accordingly.
2) If a List is intended, change the textual instructions to remove the HashSet/Set requirement and explicitly state that animals is a List (allowing duplicates), and update the UML to List<Animal>. Ensure the template and solution match the chosen type.

issues.description: The collection type used to hold Farm.animals is referenced with different identifiers across artifacts: the UML in problem_statement.md declares animals: List<Animal> while the textual requirements instruct using a Set implemented as a HashSet (unique animals). The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This inconsistency in the collection type name (List vs Set/HashSet) creates confusion about the intended data structure and semantic behavior (uniqueness/no-duplicates) students must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the collection type across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML to specify animals: Set<Animal> (and keep the textual instruction) and change the solution and template to use the Set interface and initialize a HashSet<Animal> in Farm's no-arg constructor; or (B) If List is intended, change the textual requirement to require a List and remove the HashSet/Set wording. Prefer option A to preserve the 'unique animals' requirement described in the text.
